name: Java
summary: Learn Java program structure, classes, collections, exceptions, streams, and file APIs.

lessons.title: Program entry and types
lessons.explanation: A simple Java app starts in public static void main(String[] args). Declare the type of each variable. Primitive types such as int hold values. Reference variables such as String refer to objects. Save the public class below as Main.java.

api.name: System.out.println()
api.description: Write a value followed by a line break.

api.name: Integer.parseInt(text)
api.description: Convert decimal text to an int, or throw NumberFormatException.

api.name: String.length()
api.description: Count UTF-16 code units in a string.

lessons.practice: Add a second item and print the combined total.
lessons.pitfall: When comparing String contents, use equals. The == operator tests reference identity for objects.

exercise.expected: Print a combined total for two items.
exercise.completion: Changing either quantity updates the combined total.

lessons.title: Control flow and arrays
lessons.explanation: Use if and else to choose branches. Use for-each to traverse every element or an index-based for loop when positions matter. Arrays have a fixed length and start at index zero.

api.name: array.length
api.description: Read the fixed length of an array.

api.name: Arrays.sort(array)
api.description: Sort an array in place using java.util.Arrays.

api.name: break / continue
api.description: Exit a loop or skip the remainder of its current iteration.

lessons.practice: Read a positive integer N and then N integers from stdin. Whitespace separates the values.
lessons.pitfall: The last valid array index is length minus one.

exercise.expected: Print the largest of the N integers as one line.
exercise.completion: Check all-negative values, a single item, and a repeated maximum.

lessons.title: Methods, constructors, and interfaces
lessons.explanation: Methods give an operation a name, parameters, and a return type. A constructor initializes a new object. An interface gives callers a shared contract while classes provide the implementation.

api.name: new Class(...)
api.description: Create an object and run its constructor.

api.name: this
api.description: Refer to the current instance.

api.name: @Override
api.description: Ask the compiler to confirm a method implements or overrides an existing declaration.

lessons.practice: Add another class implementing Described. Store both implementations in a Described array and print each label.
lessons.pitfall: A static method has no this reference. Pass an instance when it needs instance state.

exercise.expected: Implement two types that both implement the Described interface.
exercise.completion: A caller working only with Described prints both labels without a type check.

lessons.title: Lists, sets, and maps
lessons.explanation: List preserves sequence, Set keeps unique values, and Map looks up values by key. Declare the interface type where possible. Generics specify which object types a collection can hold.

api.name: ArrayList.add(value)
api.description: Append an item to a growable list.

api.name: HashSet.contains(value)
api.description: Test set membership.

api.name: Map.getOrDefault(key, fallback)
api.description: Read a map entry or use the fallback when the key is absent.

api.name: Map.merge(key, value, function)
api.description: Add a new value or combine it with an existing one.

lessons.practice: Count the frequency of three words and print the count for a missing word.
lessons.pitfall: List.of creates an unmodifiable list. Use an ArrayList when you need to add or remove entries.

exercise.expected: Count duplicate names and look up missing names safely.
exercise.completion: An absent key returns zero and existing counts stay intact.

lessons.title: Exceptions and resource lifetimes
lessons.explanation: Catch the specific failures you can handle. A checked exception such as IOException must be caught or declared. Try-with-resources closes an AutoCloseable object even if the block exits early.

api.name: try (resource) { ... }
api.description: Tie resource cleanup to the block scope.

api.name: throw
api.description: Raise an exception at the point of failure.

api.name: throws IOException
api.description: Tell the caller a checked exception can propagate.

lessons.practice: Change the line to a word and confirm that your numeric conversion fails gracefully.
lessons.pitfall: Avoid empty catch blocks. They hide information the caller or developer needs.

exercise.expected: Convert text to integers and handle invalid text without crashing the app.
exercise.completion: Valid text returns an int and invalid text reports a useful error.

lessons.title: Streams, lambdas, and Optional
lessons.explanation: A stream pipeline can filter and transform a collection before consuming it. Operations such as filter and map are lazy. Terminal operations such as count or toList start traversal.

api.name: Stream.filter(predicate)
api.description: Keep values satisfying a test.

api.name: Stream.map(function)
api.description: Transform each value.

api.name: Stream.findFirst()
api.description: Return an Optional with the first element, when present.

api.name: Optional.orElse(fallback)
api.description: Return the wrapped value or a default.

lessons.practice: Find the first label of length four and display a fallback if it is missing. Use Java 16 or newer for Stream.toList.
lessons.pitfall: A stream cannot be reused after its terminal operation. Create another stream from the source.

exercise.expected: Filter labels by minimum length and report a list of resulting lengths.
exercise.completion: Vary the threshold and verify the pipeline handles an empty result.

lessons.title: Paths, files, and dates
lessons.explanation: Path represents a filesystem path. Files provides operations on paths. java.time types represent calendar dates and time values without exposing mutable date fields.

api.name: Path.of(parts...)
api.description: Construct a Path from one or more strings.

api.name: Files.readString() / Files.writeString()
api.description: Read or write a small UTF-8 text file.

api.name: LocalDate.parse(text)
api.description: Parse an ISO-8601 calendar date.

lessons.practice: Write a date one month later, then read the date back. Use Java 11 or newer for the file methods.
lessons.pitfall: LocalDate has no timezone or time of day. Use an Instant or a suitable zoned type when you need a moment on the timeline.

exercise.expected: Round-trip a LocalDate through a temporary UTF-8 file.
exercise.completion: Use a date that crosses a month boundary and remove the file after the round trip.

lessons.title: Method boundaries and argument checks
lessons.explanation: A method contract describes what inputs it accepts and what result it returns. Check the conditions that the method needs before computing a result. IllegalArgumentException is useful for a caller that passes a value outside the contract.

api.name: static method
api.description: Call a class-level method without constructing an instance.

api.name: IllegalArgumentException
api.description: Signal that an argument violates the method contract.

lessons.practice: Write a method that computes a completion percentage for a positive target.
lessons.pitfall: A valid int value can still violate a domain rule. The compiler checks the type, not the application’s progress limits.

exercise.expected: Return 0 and 100 at the endpoints and reject impossible progress.
exercise.completion: Try negative, zero target, half complete, and all complete.

lessons.title: Share a generic algorithm across types
lessons.explanation: A generic method declares its type parameters before its return type. Here, the same operation reads the first element of a List<T>. The result type follows the element type, so the caller needs no unchecked cast.

api.name: <T>
api.description: Declare the element type parameter for this method.

api.name: List<T>
api.description: Accept a list whose elements have type T.

lessons.practice: Return an Optional<T> from a generic first-element method so an empty list is a normal case.
lessons.pitfall: Generic type arguments are reference types. List<Integer> uses Integer values, which Java can unbox to int.

exercise.expected: Read a string or integer when the list has elements, and return empty when it has none.
exercise.completion: Test with an empty typed list and with two different element types.

lessons.title: Model task data with records and enums
lessons.explanation: A record declares named components and supplies accessors, equality, hashCode, and a readable representation. A compact constructor can validate the component values before they are assigned. An enum restricts a status to a fixed collection of named values.

api.name: record
api.description: Declare a transparent data carrier with final component fields.

api.name: enum
api.description: Define a fixed set of named values of one type.

lessons.practice: Add an estimated-minutes component and enforce a positive duration.
lessons.pitfall: Record fields are final, but mutable objects stored in them can still change. Copy mutable components when callers must not be able to mutate the record’s state.

exercise.expected: The model accepts valid tasks and rejects blank titles or invalid durations.
exercise.completion: Check a valid task, a blank title, a missing status, and a zero-minute duration.

references.title: Java Language Specification, enum and record classes

lessons.title: Sort records by multiple keys
lessons.explanation: A Comparator defines a reusable order. Compare the primary key first, then a secondary key when the primary keys compare equally. comparingInt avoids boxing an integer key. Sorting a new ArrayList leaves the input collection’s ordering untouched.

api.name: Comparator.comparingInt()
api.description: Create a comparator from an int-valued key extractor.

api.name: thenComparing()
api.description: Apply a secondary comparison when the previous comparison returns zero.

lessons.practice: Sort tasks by descending priority and ascending title.
lessons.pitfall: Subtracting integer keys to compare them may overflow. Use comparingInt or Integer.compare.

exercise.expected: Reversing priority leaves the title tie-breaker ascending.
exercise.completion: Check negative and positive priorities and two equal-priority tasks.

lessons.title: Validate identifiers with regular expressions
lessons.explanation: Compile a Pattern once when its expression is reused. Matcher.matches checks whether the entire input matches. Matcher.find locates the next matching subsequence, which has different behavior for validation.

api.name: Pattern.compile()
api.description: Compile a regular expression.

api.name: Matcher.matches()
api.description: Test whether the complete input region matches the pattern.

lessons.practice: Validate a room code consisting of one uppercase letter, a hyphen, and two digits.
lessons.pitfall: In a Java string, a backslash needed by a regex usually must be escaped again. A literal digit class such as [0-9] avoids that extra layer.

exercise.expected: Accept only complete codes with the expected shape.
exercise.completion: Check an exact code, lowercase text, a missing separator, and text with a valid code embedded in it.

lessons.title: Publish snapshots without exposing mutable lists
lessons.explanation: List.copyOf creates an unmodifiable list with the source elements in iteration order. Editing a mutable source list afterward does not change the snapshot. This is a shallow operation, so mutable elements would still be shared.

api.name: List.copyOf()
api.description: Make an unmodifiable list from a collection of non-null elements.

api.name: new ArrayList<>(source)
api.description: Create a mutable copy of the source list structure.

lessons.practice: Take an unmodifiable snapshot of a checklist and then append an item to the live list.
lessons.pitfall: Do not confuse a live unmodifiable wrapper with a snapshot. A wrapper can reflect later changes made through the original list.

exercise.expected: The live list gains one item and the snapshot stays unchanged.
exercise.completion: Include an empty starting list, and demonstrate that adding to the snapshot is rejected.

lessons.title: Use BigDecimal for decimal amounts
lessons.explanation: BigDecimal built from text represents the decimal written in that text. Arithmetic on amounts stays decimal, and an explicit rounding mode makes a business rule visible. When scale is irrelevant, compare magnitudes with compareTo because equals also checks scale.

api.name: new BigDecimal(String)
api.description: Parse the specified decimal text exactly.

api.name: setScale()
api.description: Set a requested scale, applying the selected rounding mode if needed.

lessons.practice: Write a method to calculate a line total and round the result according to a named rule.
lessons.pitfall: Constructing BigDecimal directly from a double captures the binary floating-point approximation. Use textual input for exact decimal values.

exercise.expected: The method rounds the final total to two decimal places.
exercise.completion: Test a result already at two places and a result that needs rounding at a tie.

lessons.title: Separate reporting rules from console I/O
lessons.explanation: A reporting method is easier to test when it accepts data and returns a result. Keep printing outside the method. Grouping counts by a known enum makes absent categories explicit and prevents typos in status keys.

api.name: EnumMap
api.description: Store mappings whose keys are from one enum type.

api.name: Map.merge()
api.description: Combine a value with the current entry for a key.

lessons.practice: Use the counts method from a report that accepts a list of validated task records.
lessons.pitfall: Do not rely on the iteration order of Map.copyOf. Print keys in a chosen order when tests compare text.

exercise.expected: For an empty list the report prints zero for every supported state.
exercise.completion: Test an empty list, all tasks in one state, and tasks in mixed states.

prerequisites: Know how to save a source file.
Use a JDK 17 or newer. Save standalone examples as Main.java, then run javac Main.java and java Main.
metadata.miniProject: Build a task report. Model tasks with an enum and a record, reject blank titles, group tasks by status, and write a deterministic UTF-8 report. Test an empty list and duplicate titles.
